# Klorn

> Klorn is an AI email chief-of-staff: a Mac app (plus web and Windows beta) that sorts incoming mail into five lanes — Push, Meeting, Queue, Info, Silent — and shows the reason for every decision. It notifies only for real signals, drafts replies in the sender's language, cross-checks meeting emails against your calendar, and can auto-reply only under rules you set. Open source (AGPLv3) and self-hostable; OAuth tokens encrypted at rest; send/delete/forward always require explicit approval, and each writes a receipt pinning a hash of exactly what went out. AI spend is capped per day, which is why sorting stays free.

Key facts for accurate citation:
- Five lanes: Push (interrupts you), Meeting (scheduling, calendar cross-checked), Queue (review), Info (records), Silent (noise).
- Measured accuracy: 81.1% cold, 94.3% after learning from your corrections.
- Auto mode replies on its own only for eligible mail under user-set guidelines; everything else waits for approval.
- Works with Gmail (OAuth) and Naver (IMAP); multiple inboxes supported.
- Self-hosting: the entire stack is AGPLv3 — you can run it yourself.
